subject: Order Form opt-out playbook, notice window alignment, and MSA redlines
messages:
From: Maya Singh <maya.singh@stellarpay.com>
To: priyom_das <priyom.das@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Jordan Lowe <jordan.lowe@stellarpay.com>
Date: Tue, 7 Sep 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Initial redlines and notice window ask

Hi Priyom,

Thanks again for the demo last week — StellarPay is excited about the Dedicated offering. Attached are our suggested redlines to the MSA and Order Form. Two high-level asks from procurement and legal: 

- Opt-out/auto-renew carveout for proof-of-concept pilots (we want a 30-day notice trigger instead of 60 days for pilot accounts under $50k TCV).
- Clarify Termination for Convenience: require 60 days notice for the Order Form, but allow MSA-level termination for convenience only with customer-held credits to cover unused committed capacity.

We included a short comparison spreadsheet showing our standard terms vs Redwood's current language. Can you please loop in your legal contact and advise on what is feasible? If possible, we'd like an answer by EOD Thursday as procurement is trying to get board sign-off next week.

Attachments: StellarPay_MSA_Redlines_v2.docx (tracked), notice-window-comparison.xlsx

Thanks,
Maya
Maya Singh
Head of Procurement, StellarPay

From: priyom_das <priyom.das@redwoodinference.com>
To: Maya Singh <maya.singh@stellarpay.com>
Cc: Jordan Lowe <jordan.lowe@stellarpay.com>, karthik_iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>, laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 7 Sep 2026 16:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Initial redlines and notice window ask

Hi Maya — got the docs, thanks. Looping in Karthik (sales lead) and Laura (legal ops). A couple quick clarifying Qs from a commercial perspective before legal takes the full redline pass: 

1) Pilot carveout: is the $50k TCV threshold cumulative across renewals or per Order Form?
2) For the TFC language, are you asking that Redwood pay credits to StellarPay if Redwood terminates the MSA early (i.e., a refund/credit for remaining pre-paid committed capacity)?

We should be able to get back to you with a proposed compromise by Thursday EOD.

—Priyom
Priyom Das
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: karthik_iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
To: priyom_das <priyom.das@redwoodinference.com>, laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 8 Sep 2026 09:15:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Initial redlines and notice window ask

FW: Maya's redlines — quick internal read.

Priyom / Laura — my take: 
- Pilot carveout at $50k makes sense as a sales concession, but want it limited to the first 12 months of an Order Form and require the customer to register the pilot in our pilot program. That limits exposure.
- For TFC: we cannot broadly agree to cash refunds for termination; however, a pro-rata credit against committed capacity (usable toward future invoices) could be acceptable if we cap the maximum credit to remaining committed months up to 6 months.
- Notice windows: StellarPay asks to shorten notice to 30 days for pilots; for enterprise order forms we should keep 60 days. Maybe we counter with a 30-day option only for pilots < $50k and a clause that auto-renew triggers are disabled for those pilots.

Laura — can you confirm whether legal is comfortable with a capped pro-rata credit and the mechanics we propose? Also need to validate language to ensure we don't create an accounting liability that looks like a refund.

Karthik

From: laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
To: karthik_iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>, priyom_das <priyom.das@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 8 Sep 2026 12:28:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Initial redlines and notice window ask

On Wed, Sep 8, 2026 at 09:15 AM karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com wrote:
> FW: Maya's redlines — quick internal read.
>
> Priyom / Laura — my take: 
> - Pilot carveout at $50k makes sense as a sales concession, but want it limited to the first 12 months of an Order Form and require the customer to register the pilot in our pilot program. That limits exposure.
> - For TFC: we cannot broadly agree to cash refunds for termination; however, a pro-rata credit against committed capacity (usable toward future invoices) could be acceptable if we cap the maximum credit to remaining committed months up to 6 months.
> - Notice windows: StellarPay asks to shorten notice to 30 days for pilots; for enterprise order forms we should keep 60 days. Maybe we counter with a 30-day option only for pilots < $50k and a clause that auto-renew triggers are disabled for those pilots.

Agree with Karthik. A few legal points to include in our response: 
- Define pilot explicitly in the Order Form (start/end dates, max TCV, evaluation metrics) to avoid indefinite pilots.
- Make the pro-rata credit non-transferable and applicable only against Redwood invoices; credit should expire within 12 months of issuance.
- For accounting/ASC guidance, structure the "credit" as an account receivable reduction (customer credit note) rather than a cash refund — ops should treat it as deferred revenue adjustment.

I'll draft suggested redline snippets for the TFC and pilot carveout and attach a short clause for the Order Form that we can propose back to StellarPay.

Laura
General Counsel, Redwood Inference

From: priyom_das <priyom.das@redwoodinference.com>
To: Maya Singh <maya.singh@stellarpay.com>
Cc: Jordan Lowe <jordan.lowe@stellarpay.com>, karthik_iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>, laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 8 Sep 2026 18:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Initial redlines and notice window ask

Hi Maya — thanks for the patience while we reviewed internally. Summary of what Redwood can offer as a compromise: 

1) Pilot carveout (accept in part): Pilot definition to be included in the Order Form: max 12 months, max TCV $50,000, explicit registration via Redwood Pilot Program. For registered pilots only, customer may elect a 30-day opt-out notice and auto-renew will be disabled at the Order Form level.

2) Termination for Convenience (MSA-level): Redwood cannot provide cash refunds. Instead, we propose a capped pro-rata credit for prepaid committed capacity: credit usable only against future Redwood invoices, non-transferable, expires 12 months from issuance, and capped at remaining committed months not to exceed 6 months. Operations/legal will treat the adjustment as a customer credit note.

3) Notice windows for enterprise Order Forms remain 60 days; the 30-day pilot window is explicitly scoped only to registered pilots.

Attached: proposed redline snippets (I pulled Laura's language into a short clause) and a comparison spreadsheet for the counters. If this looks reasonable to StellarPay we can have legal team prepare an updated tracked copy or we can accept a final DocuSign with the agreed clauses.

Proposed next step: If you confirm by Fri EOD (2026-09-10), I'll have our legal team produce the tracked counter and Karthik will coordinate signature logistics.

Thanks — Priyom
---
